findings.title: Unrequested change to which secret the Studio CI job uses for credentials.
findings.body: This PR is about the listing data path (epic #2223, step 3), but this hunk changes the CI credentials. Lines 59 and 77 now read `secrets.STUDIO_READ_ACCESS_TOKEN` first and fall back to `ITERATIVE_STUDIO_READ_ACCESS_TOKEN` only when it is missing. If a `STUDIO_READ_ACCESS_TOKEN` secret exists at the org or repo level with different scope or ownership, the job will silently use it to run `git ls-remote` and to check out the private `datachain-ai/studio` repo. Neither the description nor the listing work explains this change. I can't tell from here whether that secret exists or who controls it. Move this to its own PR with a stated reason, or revert both lines to `secrets.ITERATIVE_STUDIO_READ_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

held.title: update_dataset_version now writes created_at for every caller, not just touch_reservation.
held.body:
Before this change, `update_dataset_version` skipped `created_at` along with `id`. Now any caller that passes `created_at` in `**kwargs` overwrites the version's creation time. That includes a caller that forwards a whole version's fields, such as a copy or pull that spreads `version.to_dict()`. Age-based gc, and anything that sorts or audits by creation time, would then see a changed timestamp. Only the new `touch_reservation` needs this. I can't see the other callers, so whether one passes `created_at` is unconfirmed.

Fix: keep `created_at` read-only by default and let only `touch_reservation` write it, for example with a dedicated guarded UPDATE in `touch_reservation` or an explicit opt-in flag.

held.title: New writer branch in insert_stored_rows is unused by the listing writer and changes shared behaviour.
held.body: `write_listing` always passes `sys__id` in `columns`, so it never takes this branch. The only effect is on other callers of `insert_stored_rows` whose columns omit `sys__id`. Before, those calls inserted directly with `insert_block` in batches. Now they go through `self.writer`, which may assign `sys__id` differently and send rows through the writer's parts and flush logic. The request doesn't explain this change, and it looks like a leftover from an earlier attempt. Either drop it or explain it in the PR.
